global_issues.title: Hot US jobs data lifts Fed hike odds, stocks fall
global_issues.note: Confirmed: August nonfarm payrolls beat estimates (+162k vs ~55k expected), unemployment steady at 4.1%. CME FedWatch odds of a 25bp hike at the Sept 15-16 meeting rose to ~60-65%. Dow -0.51%, S&P -0.38%, Nasdaq -0.29% on the Sept 4 close, consistent with briefing's framing.

global_issues.title: US weighs 100% tariffs on Korean memory chips
global_issues.note: Materially incomplete as of briefing time. Commerce Secretary Lutnick's 100% tariff threat is real, but South Korea's top trade envoy Yeo Han-koo (Reuters, early Sept) stated Samsung and SK Hynix specifically will NOT face the full 100% tariff, citing their US fab investments (Samsung Texas, SK Hynix Indiana) under the Seoul-Washington trade deal. The briefing's 'policy overhang widened' framing misses this de-escalation for the two named companies.

sector_check.note: MU strength aligns with real blowout Q3 results and ~$100B in binding HBM/AI memory contracts sold out through 2026; NVDA/MSFT/CRWD AI-infra leadership and TSLA/GOOGL rate-sensitive laggard framing are consistent with reported conditions. grok_report.summary: The briefing's core narrative (hot jobs data → higher Fed hike odds → equity selloff, AI-memory/infra leadership vs rate-sensitive laggards) is well-supported by current reporting. Its main shortcoming is the tariff issue: it omits South Korea's trade envoy statement that Samsung and SK Hynix will not face the full 100% chip tariff, which meaningfully softens the 'policy overhang' framing used to explain sector rotation.
